observations: Photo 0, 1, 2 show a disassembled used engine and transmission assembly lying on wet pavement, with front struts/coil springs still attached on both sides.
Black plastic engine cover is visible in all three photos with two small holes and raised lettering, but no readable brand or model text is legible in any photo.
Red plastic strips cover what appear to be fuel injector connectors along one side of the engine.
A watermark reading 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' appears across photos 0 and 2 - this is the seller's business name/watermark, not a vehicle brand marking.
Background in photo 1 shows other engines and parts stacked in what looks like a scrapyard or spare-parts lot.
No VIN plate, engine code sticker, odometer, dashboard, or any running/test video is visible in any photo.
Surfaces show dirt, grime, and corrosion on metal brackets and bolts, consistent with a used, unwashed pull.
Seller's new message is text only, reasserting prior claims; no new photo or video was provided.

identity.kind: used car engine and transmission assembly with attached front struts (spare parts)

claims.evidence: No shipping documents, customs paperwork, or container/port photos shown in any of the 3 photos.
No video or audio of the engine running is provided; seller's verbal reassurance is not visual proof.
Cannot be assessed from static photos; requires a running audio/video clip, still not supplied.
No odometer photo, service sticker, or mileage documentation visible in any photo.
No seal, gasket close-up, or bolt-torque marks shown to confirm the engine has not been disassembled.

claims.claim: 'I tested it myself yesterday, everything I said is true'
claims.evidence: A verbal assurance with no accompanying photo or video; words from the seller are not evidence per the evaluation rules.

risks.risk: Engine may not actually run or may knock/smoke once installed
risks.proof: A clear video clip of the engine running (cold start, idle, and revved) with audible sound
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / non-running core

risks.risk: Mileage is unknown and could be high despite claim
risks.proof: Photo of odometer or original vehicle dashboard, or dealer mileage certificate

risks.risk: Make/model/engine code cannot be confirmed, so fitment to buyer's car is unverifiable
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code plate, casting number, or chassis/VIN tag
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified generic used engine, not matched to any specific vehicle

risks.risk: Wiring harness, sensors, or ECU may be missing or cut, common in yard-pulled engines
risks.proof: Wide photo showing the full wiring harness from engine to firewall connector, undamaged

risks.risk: Internal damage (cracked block, bent valves) hidden by the engine cover
risks.proof: Photo with the plastic engine cover removed, showing the bare cylinder head and block
risks.if_unproven: priced as risk of hidden internal damage

risks.risk: Attached struts/suspension parts may be worn or mismatched, inflating perceived value
risks.proof: Close-up of strut mounting bushings and spring condition
risks.if_unproven: priced as used/worn suspension components bundled in, not a premium add-on

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/casting number or chassis VIN tag to confirm make, model, and displacement
Video of the engine running (start-up, idle, rev) with clear audio, filmed now, not a past claim
Photo of the odometer or any mileage documentation from the donor vehicle
Wide shot showing the complete wiring harness and connectors attached to the engine
Photo with the engine cover removed to inspect the cylinder head/block for cracks or damage
response.reason: The seller's reply adds only verbal reassurance with no new photo or video, so the identity and all condition claims remain unverifiable; a worst-case price still cannot be anchored without the engine code and a running proof.
